hero.title: Explore what is happening above, on and beneath the surface.
hero.subtitle: Explore the changing Baltic Sea through scientific models, historical assessments and environmental data.
hero.body: This public prototype combines marine science, environmental context and an interactive map so more people can understand the sea as a living system rather than a technical dataset.

preview.title: Whole Baltic Sea
preview.body: Explore published Baltic-wide ocean model data and historical environmental context.

sections.whatTitle: Different layers come from different kinds of knowledge.
sections.layersTitle: A public-facing platform for the whole Baltic Sea.
sections.layersBody: The map includes available ocean-condition datasets and historical reference layers. Planned integrations are labelled Coming soon.
sections.accessibilityTitle: Choose a temperature colour scale that is easier to read.
sections.accessibilityBody: The map keeps the same data while the colour palette changes. This makes it easier to compare the sea in different viewing conditions, including colour-vision differences.
sections.whyTitle: A sea that is enclosed, connected and vulnerable.
sections.sourcesKicker: Where does the information come from?
sections.sourcesTitle: Scientific sources remain visible, but secondary to exploration.

observed.title: Observed
observed.body: Measured by instruments, monitoring stations or surveys.

modelled.title: Modelled
modelled.body: Scientific models estimating ocean conditions at the selected model time.

historical.title: Historical
historical.body: Monitoring records that reveal how the sea changes over time.

enclosed.title: Almost enclosed
enclosed.body: Water exchange is limited, so changes can linger for years.

gradient.title: Strong gradients
gradient.body: Salinity, temperature and ecology shift dramatically across the region.

pressure.title: Human pressure
pressure.body: Shipping, nutrients, contaminants and fishing all shape the sea.

change.title: Climate change
change.body: Warming, oxygen depletion and ecosystem change are already visible.

sources.future: Additional Baltic data sources as layers are added

map.layersCaption: Available layers can be explored now. Planned layers are labelled Coming soon.
map.noiseCaption: HELCOM assessment layers and reported impulsive events are shown as environmental context, not live sound measurements.
map.infrastructureCaption: Ports, energy, routes and land-use context stay available while ocean data move through time.
map.noOverlaySubtitle: Select an overlay to explore the Baltic Sea

status.fallbackMap: The basemap could not be loaded. The map uses the published coastline mask where available.

transparency.noiseDetail: Assessment pressure layers and reported impulsive-noise events
transparency.noiseCaution: Continuous and impulsive metrics are shown separately and are not combined into one number.
transparency.noiseReporting: Reported events depend on national reporting completeness.
